_comment: Indexable HEX pages (tools/build-color-pages.js). Every other /color/hex/ page is noindex, follow and stays out of sitemap-colors.xml. kind: css = CSS named color, popular = common color name searched without a CSS keyword, brand = widely cited brand color. note = 1–2 sentences on the name's origin or a notable fact; palette, web and print lines are computed.

colors.name: Alice Blue
colors.note: Named after Alice Roosevelt Longworth, daughter of Theodore Roosevelt, whose pale blue-grey gowns set a fashion in the early 1900s. It reached CSS through the X11 color list.

colors.name: Antique White
colors.note: A warm off-white meant to evoke aged paper and old lace, adopted into CSS from the X11 color list.

colors.name: Aqua / Cyan
colors.note: Full green plus full blue light with no red. 'Aqua' is the HTML 4 name and 'cyan' the printing name; both keywords give the same value, and cyan is also one of the four CMYK process inks.

colors.name: Aquamarine
colors.note: Named after the blue-green beryl gemstone, whose name comes from the Latin aqua marina, 'sea water'.

colors.name: Azure
colors.note: From the Persian word for lapis lazuli via Old French azur. In CSS it is an almost-white pale cyan, much lighter than the deep blue 'azure' of heraldry.

colors.name: Beige
colors.note: From the French word for natural, undyed wool. A staple neutral for backgrounds, interiors and packaging.

colors.name: Bisque
colors.note: Named after bisque (biscuit) ware, unglazed pottery fired once, which has this pale peach tone.

colors.name: Black
colors.note: On screen black is the absence of light: every RGB channel at zero. One of the 16 original HTML color names.

colors.name: Blanched Almond
colors.note: The pale cream of an almond after blanching removes its brown skin; one of the food-inspired names from the X11 list.

colors.name: Blue
colors.note: The pure blue primary of the sRGB model, with only the blue channel lit. One of the 16 original HTML color names.

colors.name: Blue Violet
colors.note: A saturated violet that sits between blue and purple; inherited by CSS from the X11 list.

colors.name: Brown
colors.note: The CSS keyword 'brown' is a fairly red, brick-like brown rather than a chocolate tone, a value inherited from the X11 list.

colors.name: Burlywood
colors.note: Named after the light tan of burl wood, the knotted growths on tree trunks that woodworkers prize for veneers.

colors.name: Cadet Blue
colors.note: A muted grey-blue associated with military cadet uniforms; kept in CSS from the X11 list.

colors.name: Chartreuse
colors.note: Named after Chartreuse, the herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks since the 18th century, whose green version has this yellow-green hue.

colors.name: Chocolate
colors.note: Despite the name, CSS 'chocolate' is a bright reddish brown that reads closer to cinnamon or rust than to dark chocolate.

colors.name: Coral
colors.note: Named after the pinkish orange of red coral. A similar shade, 'Living Coral', was Pantone's Color of the Year for 2019.

colors.name: Cornflower Blue
colors.note: Named after the cornflower (Centaurea cyanus). Game developers know it as the default clear color in Microsoft XNA project templates.

colors.name: Cornsilk
colors.note: The pale yellow of the silky threads at the tip of an ear of corn.

colors.name: Crimson
colors.note: From the kermes insect dye (Arabic qirmiz). A deep red long used for ceremonial robes, flags and university colors.

colors.name: Dark Blue
colors.note: Blue at a little over half intensity: a deep, ink-like blue that keeps strong contrast with white text.

colors.name: Dark Cyan
colors.note: Cyan at about 55% intensity, giving a dark teal often used for links and accents on light backgrounds.

colors.name: Dark Goldenrod
colors.note: A darker, browner relative of goldenrod, named after the yellow-flowered Solidago plant.

colors.name: Dark Gray
colors.note: A famous CSS quirk: 'darkgray' is lighter than plain 'gray' (#808080), because the X11 and HTML color lists were merged without reconciling them.

colors.name: Dark Green
colors.note: A deep natural green with the green channel at about 39%, darker than the CSS keyword 'green'.

colors.name: Dark Khaki
colors.note: A deeper version of khaki, a word from Hindi-Urdu meaning 'dust-colored', first used for British army uniforms in India.

colors.name: Dark Magenta
colors.note: Magenta at about 55% intensity: a rich plum-purple.

colors.name: Dark Olive Green
colors.note: A muted khaki-green in the same family as military olive drab, popular for outdoor and natural themes.

colors.name: Dark Orange
colors.note: A deeper, more saturated orange than the CSS keyword 'orange', often used for warning and call-to-action accents.

colors.name: Dark Orchid
colors.note: A darker, more saturated variant of orchid, named after the orchid flower.

colors.name: Dark Red
colors.note: Red at about 55% intensity: a deep blood or wine red.

colors.name: Dark Salmon
colors.note: A muted pink-orange named after the color of salmon flesh, slightly deeper than CSS 'salmon'.

colors.name: Dark Sea Green
colors.note: A soft, greyish green meant to suggest shallow sea water; useful as a calm accent.

colors.name: Dark Slate Blue
colors.note: A dark blue-violet named after the bluish tone of slate rock.

colors.name: Dark Slate Gray
colors.note: A very dark grey-green, often used as a softer alternative to pure black for body text and dark UI.

colors.name: Dark Turquoise
colors.note: A strong blue-green named after the turquoise gemstone, deeper than CSS 'turquoise'.

colors.name: Dark Violet
colors.note: A vivid violet with no green component, close to the violet end of the visible spectrum.

colors.name: Deep Pink
colors.note: A loud, saturated pink with full red and strong blue; one of the most vivid pinks in the CSS list.

colors.name: Deep Sky Blue
colors.note: A bright, clear blue meant to recall a cloudless midday sky, more saturated than 'skyblue'.

colors.name: Dim Gray
colors.note: A dark neutral grey (105 in every channel), darker than both 'gray' and 'darkgray'.

colors.name: Dodger Blue
colors.note: A bright azure commonly linked to the blue of the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team; it reached CSS through the X11 list.

colors.name: Firebrick
colors.note: Named after the red of fired clay bricks; a strong, slightly brown red.

colors.name: Floral White
colors.note: A barely warm off-white, like the petals of white flowers; popular for paper-like page backgrounds.

colors.name: Forest Green
colors.note: A medium-dark green meant to suggest the canopy of a forest; widely used for nature and outdoor brands.

colors.name: Fuchsia / Magenta
colors.note: Fuchsia is named after the fuchsia flower (itself named for botanist Leonhart Fuchs); magenta after an aniline dye named for the 1859 Battle of Magenta. Both keywords give full red plus full blue.

colors.name: Gainsboro
colors.note: A light grey named after the English painter Thomas Gainsborough, spelled as it appeared in the X11 list.

colors.name: Ghost White
colors.note: A white with the faintest blue tint, useful for cool, clean page backgrounds.

colors.name: Gold
colors.note: A bright golden yellow standing in for metallic gold, which screens can only suggest with flat color or gradients.

colors.name: Goldenrod
colors.note: Named after goldenrod (Solidago), a North American wildflower with dense yellow flower heads.

colors.name: Gray
colors.note: Exactly 128 in each channel, the mid-point of the 0–255 range. CSS accepts both spellings, 'gray' and 'grey'.

colors.name: Green
colors.note: CSS 'green' is only half intensity (#008000). The full-brightness #00FF00 is called 'lime', a legacy of the original 16 HTML color names.

colors.name: Green Yellow
colors.note: A bright yellow-green, between chartreuse and yellow, that reads as fresh and electric on screen.

colors.name: Honeydew
colors.note: Named after the pale green flesh of the honeydew melon.

colors.name: Hot Pink
colors.note: A bold, playful pink that became a pop-culture staple; brighter and warmer than 'deeppink'.

colors.name: Indian Red
colors.note: Named after a red iron-oxide earth pigment historically imported from India.

colors.name: Indigo
colors.note: Named after the blue dye from Indigofera plants. Isaac Newton included indigo as one of the seven colors of the rainbow.

colors.name: Ivory
colors.note: The warm off-white of elephant tusk ivory; a classic choice for wedding stationery and soft backgrounds.

colors.name: Khaki
colors.note: From the Hindi-Urdu word for 'dust-colored'. Note that CSS 'khaki' is a pale yellow, lighter than the khaki of most uniforms.

colors.name: Lavender
colors.note: Named after the pale purple flowers of the lavender plant; a soft, calming tint.

colors.name: Lavender Blush
colors.note: An almost-white with a faint pink-lavender tint, as if lavender were blushing.

colors.name: Lawn Green
colors.note: A vivid yellow-green suggesting freshly cut grass.

colors.name: Lemon Chiffon
colors.note: Named after lemon chiffon pie, with its light, pale-yellow filling.

colors.name: Light Blue
colors.note: A soft pastel blue, darker and more saturated than 'aliceblue' or 'azure'.

colors.name: Light Coral
colors.note: A soft pinkish red, lighter and pinker than CSS 'coral'.

colors.name: Light Cyan
colors.note: A very pale cyan, close to white with a cool aqua tint.

colors.name: Light Goldenrod Yellow
colors.note: At 20 letters, 'lightgoldenrodyellow' is the longest CSS color keyword.

colors.name: Light Gray
colors.note: A light neutral grey (211 in each channel), common for borders, dividers and disabled controls.

colors.name: Light Green
colors.note: A soft pastel green, slightly deeper than 'palegreen'.

colors.name: Light Pink
colors.note: Another CSS quirk: 'lightpink' is slightly darker and more saturated than plain 'pink' (#FFC0CB).

colors.name: Light Salmon
colors.note: A light orange-pink named after salmon flesh, more orange than 'salmon'.

colors.name: Light Sea Green
colors.note: Despite 'light' in the name, this is a medium teal, darker than 'mediumaquamarine'.

colors.name: Light Sky Blue
colors.note: A soft daytime-sky blue, slightly more saturated than 'skyblue'.

colors.name: Light Slate Gray
colors.note: A blue-tinted mid grey named after slate rock, popular for secondary text.

colors.name: Light Steel Blue
colors.note: A pale grey-blue suggesting polished steel.

colors.name: Light Yellow
colors.note: A very pale yellow, close to cream; useful for highlights and notes.

colors.name: Lime
colors.note: The full green channel of sRGB. HTML named it 'lime' because the keyword 'green' was already used for the darker #008000.

colors.name: Lime Green
colors.note: A bright but slightly softer green than 'lime', named after the citrus fruit.

colors.name: Linen
colors.note: The off-white of undyed linen cloth woven from flax.

colors.name: Maroon
colors.note: From the French marron, 'chestnut'. A deep brownish red and one of the 16 original HTML color names.

colors.name: Medium Aquamarine
colors.note: A muted, minty blue-green named after the aquamarine gemstone.

colors.name: Medium Blue
colors.note: Blue at about 80% intensity, between 'blue' and 'darkblue'.

colors.name: Medium Orchid
colors.note: A medium purple-pink named after orchid flowers.

colors.name: Medium Purple
colors.note: A soft lavender-purple, lighter and bluer than CSS 'purple'.

colors.name: Medium Sea Green
colors.note: A balanced medium green with a hint of blue, often used for success states.

colors.name: Medium Slate Blue
colors.note: A bright periwinkle-violet, named after the bluish tone of slate.

colors.name: Medium Spring Green
colors.note: A vivid mint green suggesting new spring growth.

colors.name: Medium Turquoise
colors.note: A medium blue-green named after the turquoise gemstone.

colors.name: Medium Violet Red
colors.note: A deep magenta-pink between violet and red.

colors.name: Midnight Blue
colors.note: A very dark navy suggesting the night sky; a favorite for dark themes and formal designs.

colors.name: Mint Cream
colors.note: A near-white with a cool mint tint.

colors.name: Misty Rose
colors.note: A pale, dusty pink, like a rose seen through mist.

colors.name: Moccasin
colors.note: Named after the soft tan of deerskin moccasin shoes.

colors.name: Navajo White
colors.note: A warm, pale tan from the X11 list. Developers like to point out that its hex code, FFDEAD, spells 'dead'.

colors.name: Navy
colors.note: Named after the dark blue uniforms the British Royal Navy adopted in the 18th century. One of the 16 original HTML color names.

colors.name: Old Lace
colors.note: The warm off-white of aged lace; a gentle alternative to pure white.

colors.name: Olive
colors.note: The dull yellow-green of unripe olives; one of the 16 original HTML color names.

colors.name: Olive Drab
colors.note: Associated with the olive drab used on US military uniforms and equipment in the 20th century.

colors.name: Orange
colors.note: Named after the fruit. 'orange' was added in CSS 2.1 as the 17th standard color keyword.

colors.name: Orange Red
colors.note: A vivid red-orange, the color behind many alert and accent designs.

colors.name: Orchid
colors.note: A light purple-pink named after the orchid flower.

colors.name: Pale Goldenrod
colors.note: A light, soft yellow, a paler form of goldenrod.

colors.name: Pale Green
colors.note: A light, fresh pastel green.

colors.name: Pale Turquoise
colors.note: A light, airy blue-green named after turquoise.

colors.name: Pale Violet Red
colors.note: A dusty rose pink between violet and red.

colors.name: Papaya Whip
colors.note: Named after a dessert of whipped papaya; a pale peach cream.

colors.name: Peach Puff
colors.note: A soft peach suggesting a powder puff; popular for gentle, warm backgrounds.

colors.name: Peru
colors.note: A light reddish brown kept in CSS from the X11 color list.

colors.name: Pink
colors.note: The color is named after pinks (Dianthus) — flowers whose frilled petals look as if cut with pinking shears.

colors.name: Plum
colors.note: A light purple named after the fruit, though much paler than a ripe plum's skin.

colors.name: Powder Blue
colors.note: A soft, chalky pale blue, popular for nurseries, calm interfaces and spring palettes.

colors.name: Purple
colors.note: Long linked to royalty because Tyrian purple dye was so costly. One of the 16 original HTML color names.

colors.name: Rebecca Purple
colors.note: Added in CSS Color Level 4 in 2014 in memory of Rebecca Meyer, the daughter of CSS pioneer Eric Meyer.

colors.name: Red
colors.note: The pure red primary of sRGB, with only the red channel lit. One of the 16 original HTML color names.

colors.name: Rosy Brown
colors.note: A greyish dusty rose, somewhere between pink and brown.

colors.name: Royal Blue
colors.note: A rich, vivid blue traditionally associated with royal households and formal uniforms.

colors.name: Saddle Brown
colors.note: The warm brown of tanned leather saddles.

colors.name: Salmon
colors.note: Named after the pink-orange color of salmon flesh.

colors.name: Sandy Brown
colors.note: A light orange-brown evoking beach sand.

colors.name: Sea Green
colors.note: A medium-dark green with a blue tint, suggesting deep sea water.

colors.name: Seashell
colors.note: A warm white with a pinkish tint, like the inside of a seashell.

colors.name: Sienna
colors.note: Named after the earth pigment from the area around Siena, Italy, used by painters since the Renaissance.

colors.name: Silver
colors.note: A light grey standing in for metallic silver; one of the 16 original HTML color names.

colors.name: Sky Blue
colors.note: The soft blue of a clear daytime sky; a staple for light, friendly designs.

colors.name: Slate Blue
colors.note: A medium blue-violet named after the bluish tone of slate rock.

colors.name: Slate Gray
colors.note: A cool grey with a blue tint named after slate; common for secondary text and icons.

colors.name: Snow
colors.note: A white with the faintest warm tint, like fresh snow.

colors.name: Spring Green
colors.note: In color theory 'spring green' sits exactly between green and cyan on the color wheel.

colors.name: Steel Blue
colors.note: A medium blue-grey suggesting tempered steel; a versatile corporate blue.

colors.name: Tan
colors.note: Named after tanbark, the oak bark used to tan leather.

colors.name: Teal
colors.note: Named after the common teal, a duck with a blue-green stripe around its eye. One of the 16 original HTML color names.

colors.name: Thistle
colors.note: A pale greyish purple named after thistle flowers.

colors.name: Tomato
colors.note: A bright red-orange named after ripe tomatoes; a popular warm accent.

colors.name: Turquoise
colors.note: Named after the gemstone, from the French for 'Turkish', as the stone reached Europe through Turkey.

colors.name: Violet
colors.note: CSS 'violet' is a light pinkish purple, much paler than the violet end of the visible spectrum.

colors.name: Wheat
colors.note: The pale golden beige of ripe wheat.

colors.name: White
colors.note: All three RGB channels at full intensity. In print, white is simply the unprinted paper.

colors.name: White Smoke
colors.note: A very light grey (245 in each channel), a common subtle background behind white cards.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.note: Full red plus full green light. Yellow is also one of the four CMYK process inks.

colors.name: Yellow Green
colors.note: A medium yellow-green between olive and lime.

colors.name: Pastel Pink
colors.note: A soft, light pink and one of the most searched pastel tones, used for baby products, cosmetics and gentle UI accents.

colors.name: Pastel Blue
colors.note: A muted, greyish light blue that keeps a calm, airy feel in pastel palettes.

colors.name: Pastel Green
colors.note: A soft but clearly green pastel, often paired with pastel pink and yellow in spring palettes.

colors.name: Pastel Yellow
colors.note: A gentle, buttery yellow that adds warmth without the glare of pure yellow.

colors.name: Pastel Purple
colors.note: A dusty, greyed lavender common in pastel and vintage-inspired palettes.

colors.name: Baby Blue
colors.note: A light blue traditionally used for baby clothing and nurseries.

colors.name: Mint Green
colors.note: A fresh, light green named after mint leaves; associated with cleanliness and freshness.

colors.name: Sage Green
colors.note: A grey-green named after the leaves of the sage herb; a long-running favorite in interior and wedding design.

colors.name: Burgundy
colors.note: Named after the red wine of the Burgundy region of France; a deep, purple-tinted red.

colors.name: Mustard Yellow
colors.note: A warm, slightly dull yellow named after prepared mustard; popular in fashion and retro designs.

colors.name: Cream
colors.note: The pale yellowish white of dairy cream; softer than pure white for paper-like designs.

colors.name: Charcoal
colors.note: A dark blue-grey named after burnt wood charcoal; a softer alternative to black for text and dark themes.

colors.name: Emerald
colors.note: Named after the green beryl gemstone. Pantone chose Emerald as its Color of the Year for 2013.

colors.name: Ruby
colors.note: A deep pinkish red named after the ruby gemstone, a variety of the mineral corundum.

colors.name: Rose Gold
colors.note: A pinkish metallic tone from gold–copper alloys; on screen it is shown as this flat dusty rose.

colors.name: Champagne
colors.note: A pale golden beige named after the sparkling wine; common in wedding and luxury design.

colors.name: Mauve
colors.note: From the French name of the mallow flower. Mauveine, the first synthetic dye (1856), made the color a sensation.

colors.name: Terracotta
colors.note: From the Italian for 'baked earth', the orange-brown of unglazed fired clay.

colors.name: Peach
colors.note: The pale orange of peach flesh. Pantone named 'Peach Fuzz' its Color of the Year for 2024.

colors.name: Lilac
colors.note: A pale purple named after the flowers of the lilac shrub (Syringa).

colors.name: Cobalt Blue
colors.note: Named after the cobalt-based pigment used in Chinese porcelain and by painters since the early 19th century.

colors.name: Neon Green
colors.note: An extremely bright green that sits at the edge of what screens can show; it will look duller when printed.

colors.name: Facebook Blue
colors.note: Widely cited as the brand blue of Facebook since its 2019 brand refresh.

colors.name: Twitter Blue
colors.note: The light blue long used by Twitter before its 2023 rebrand to X.

colors.name: Spotify Green
colors.note: Widely cited as the brand green of Spotify.

colors.name: Netflix Red
colors.note: Widely cited as the brand red of Netflix.

colors.name: Google Blue
colors.note: The blue of Google's four-color logo palette, alongside #EA4335, #FBBC05 and #34A853.

colors.name: LinkedIn Blue
colors.note: Widely cited as the brand blue of LinkedIn.

colors.name: WhatsApp Green
colors.note: Widely cited as the brand green of WhatsApp.

colors.name: Discord Blurple
colors.note: Discord calls its signature blue-purple 'Blurple'; this is the value from its 2021 refresh.

colors.name: Amazon Orange
colors.note: Widely cited as the orange of the Amazon smile logo.

colors.name: Starbucks Green
colors.note: Widely cited as the brand green of Starbucks.

colors.name: Kakao Yellow
colors.note: The yellow used for KakaoTalk and Kakao login buttons in Korea.

colors.name: Naver Green
colors.note: The green used for Naver's logo and login buttons in Korea.

colors.name: Tiffany Blue
colors.note: A common screen approximation of the robin's-egg blue associated with Tiffany & Co.; the official color is a trademarked custom Pantone shade.

colors.name: Pinterest Red
colors.note: Widely cited as the brand red of Pinterest.

colors.name: Twitch Purple
colors.note: Widely cited as the brand purple of Twitch since its 2019 rebrand.
